To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed an attack space defined by system knowledge, disclosure and disruption resources and that we modeled, analyzed, experimentally illustrated, and provided counter-measures for three attack scenarios.

(i) a framework to analyze attacks on cyber-secure networked controls is proposed; (ii) three attack scenarios, namely, replay, zero dynamics and bias injection attacks, are modeled using this framework and are illustrated experimentally; and (iii) the proposed framework is used to analyze the consequences of the attack scenarios and to propose counter-measures to mitigate the attacks.

we have developed a general attack model for networked control that allows us to analyze and experimentally validate replay, zero dynamics and bias injection attacks, and that the proposed attack model can be used to analyze and experiment attacks on networked control systems with a wide range of architectures and communication protocols.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework for the modeling, analysis and experimental evaluation of attacks on networked control systems and their counter-measures.
the analysis and mitigation of attacks against cyber-physical systems.
the analysis and mitigation of cyber-physical attacks on networked control systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the attack space is defined and the attack scenarios and consequences have been modeled and illustrated.
this paper provides a very good and comprehensive overview of the state of the art in the area of cyber-security for Networked Control Systems.
cyber security is an important aspect of the design, development, and deployment of networked control systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have introduced an attack model for networked control that is applicable for a broad range of attacks, we have shown how this model can be applied for analyzing attack scenarios for networked systems, and we have demonstrated the model and its application using a wireless networked control system.
a networked control architecture is inherently more vulnerable to attacks compared to a centralized control architecture.
we have shown how the attack space can be used to model attacks, and how the resulting attack models can be used to identify the most effective counter-measures.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the attack scenarios can be modeled as linear time-invariant systems, and that the adversary's attack capabilities are constrained by his system knowledge, disclosure resources, and disruption capabilities.
the attack space is defined by adversary resources.
the attack space is a useful framework for analyzing the consequences of cyber-security threats on networked control systems.
